findings.title: Live read during ~forward_scope sees forwards one ahead of token_jobs and the path-set histogram; only the three job counts are documented as consistent
findings.trigger: A FUSE reader (the single FUSE worker thread, doc/fuse_stats_design.md:118) reads <class>_forwards while the main thread is inside ~forward_scope. Inside ~forward_scope, note_forward_wall runs first (attn_stats.hpp:881). Then end_forward increments token_jobs_by_path_set once per job (attn_stats.hpp:566-576), and only then adds token_jobs (attn_stats.hpp:581).
findings.consequence: During that window a read can show forwards = N+1 with token_jobs of N forwards, and sum(token_jobs_by_path_set) larger than token_jobs by up to one forward's jobs. Both are transient and correct after the fold (the per-job loop in end_forward, attn_stats.hpp:566-576). README.stats.md:255-261 and attn_stats.hpp:577-579 document only the three job counts. A reader who computes per-forward averages or checks sum(histogram) == token_jobs from a live read can see a false mismatch.
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:879-883: "~forward_scope() noexcept { if (!on) return; stats.note_forward_wall(...); stats.end_forward(n_token_jobs); }"
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:543-544: "fc.forwards.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed); fc.wall_cycles.fetch_add(cycles, ...)"
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:575: "fc.token_jobs_by_path_set[set].fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);" (inside the per-job loop, before line 581 "fc.token_jobs.fetch_add(n_token_jobs, ...)")
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:577-579: "The three job counts move together, in three relaxed adds. A read between them can differ ... A read at any other time sees the equality."
findings.discriminating_check: Poll <class>_forwards at high rate during a long prefill forward (a forward over prompt tokens): a sample with forwards == token_jobs-derived count + 1, or sum(token_jobs_by_path_set) > token_jobs, shows the window. A documented statement would make it acceptable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to README.stats.md:255-261 and the Note at attn_stats.hpp:577-579: "forwards and wall_cycles are added before the fold, and the histogram before token_jobs. So a read during the fold can show forwards ahead by one, and the histogram sum ahead of token_jobs by one forward's jobs." Optionally add token_jobs before the histogram loop so the histogram never leads it.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Confirmed at HEAD: the fold loop at attn_stats.hpp:566-576 runs n_token_jobs iterations before token_jobs is added at :581. So the histogram-ahead window is one loop over all jobs of the forward (long for a prefill forward). forwards (:543) leads token_jobs for all of end_forward. evidence: Confirmed at HEAD: forwards/wall_cycles are added before the fold loop, and the path-set histogram is filled inside it. So a FUSE read during ~forward_scope (render_forwards loads each atomic separately, attn_stats.hpp:760-787) can show forwards one ahead of token_jobs, and sum(histogram) > token_jobs by one forward's jobs. The window is the whole fold loop (jobs x attention rows), not "a few instructions". The README and Note make no wrong claim. They only omit this. So nit/doc gap holds. A reorder of token_jobs ahead of the histogram loop would not close the forwards lead. The reason is that note_forward_wall runs first.
intent: Holds as a documentation gap, not a wrong-number defect. The window is only the fold loop inside ~forward_scope (microseconds est.). Every counter is correct once it ends. The README's consistency promise covers only the three job counts. Adopt only the one-sentence doc fix. Moving token_jobs before the histogram loop would break the documented 'three counts move together' property.

findings.title: 'T2 minus T5 is compute plus fold' omits the output_channel.start_writing barrier wait inside T2
findings.trigger: Any layer where an attention worker reaches output_channel.start_writing (self_attention.hpp:840) before the main thread has prepared that channel for the layer. In the llama plugin (the tron model implementation in llama.hpp) the next layer's WQ (the query-projection matrix multiply) is launched (llama.hpp:686, async case) before next_layer() (llama.hpp:695) calls vo_channel.prepare() (llama.hpp:1555). prepare() itself waits for the previous layer's WO (the output-projection matrix multiply) to finish reading vo (the buffer that carries the attention output to WO) (common.hpp:540-545, threading.hpp:951-963, llama.hpp:1156-1163).
findings.consequence: The wait in start_writing (common.hpp:550-552 -> barrier::wait, threading.hpp:966-968, a blocking wait_until_geq) lies inside the T2 window (self_attention.hpp:832 to 853) and is not part of T5. README.stats.md:289-290 and attn_stats.hpp:43 tell the reader that T2 - T5 is compute plus fold. A reader attributes this wait to attention compute. The Note's definition of T2 at attn_stats.hpp:33-35 ("both passes and the join, without the upstream K/V wait") is also incomplete for the same reason. Magnitude not measured. Insufficient data: a perfetto trace (perfetto is the event-tracing tool that tron's TRACE_EVENT macros write to) with the "vo" channel wait would give it.
findings.discriminating_check: Perfetto trace of a llama-plugin decode run: look for a gap between the end of "Attention Pending" and the start of "attention: join" on an attention worker (the start_writing wait). Compare that gap with join_wait_cycles for that layer. If the gap is non-zero while T5 is zero, the doc sentence is wrong as stated. Alternatively add a temporary rdtsc pair (rdtsc is the CPU instruction that reads the time-stamp counter) around line 840 and print the sum.
findings.suggested_fix: Change README.stats.md:290 and attn_stats.hpp:43 to: "T2 minus T5 is compute plus fold plus the wait for the output buffer (output_channel.start_writing), which is not timed." Extend the T2 definition at attn_stats.hpp:33-35 and worker_layer_row's comment at 229-231 the same way. Do not move start_writing out of the T2 window: attn_elapsed also feeds record_attention_time (llama.hpp:775, model.hpp:2147-2155).
lenses: TIMERS T2..T5 (rdtsc (the CPU instruction that reads the time-stamp counter) placement, units, observer worker, minibatch (a slice of the forward's tokens processed as one unit) and last-layer behavior, T5 double-count and exit paths, switch-off cost) in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp and h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp at HEAD 04da001cb5 (rdtsc is the CPU instruction that reads the time-stamp counter)

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds: the only untimed blocking wait inside the T2 window is output_channel.start_writing (self_attention.hpp:840). query_channel.start_reading (:811) and rope's start_writing are outside T2. The finish_* / done calls at :849-851 do not block. The window shape is inherited from the base commit. So the fix is to the three doc sentences (README.stats.md:290, attn_stats.hpp:33-35 and :43, :229-231), not to the rdtsc (the CPU instruction that reads the time-stamp counter) placement. The magnitude of the wait is unmeasured.
evidence: Confirmed at HEAD: the output_channel.start_writing barrier wait (self_attention.hpp:840, a blocking wait_until_geq via common.hpp:552 / threading.hpp:967) lies inside the T2 window (832-853) and outside both T5 accumulation points (1152, 1282). So "T2 minus T5 is compute plus fold" is incomplete. The wait is reachable in the llama plugin. The reason is that run_attention_worker never calls wait_for_layer, and vo_channel.prepare() runs only at next_layer (llama.hpp:695) after launch_wq (686). Its size is unmeasured (channel comment common.hpp:334-336 calls it "usually a non-wait"). So this is a doc fix, not a timer bug.
intent: The start_writing barrier does sit inside T2 and outside T5. So the sentence is imprecise. In the llama plugin the barrier cannot block for KV-writing operations. The pending pass at self_attention.hpp:830 already waited for this layer's save_k/save_v. The main thread launches those (llama.hpp:702) only after vo_channel.prepare() (llama.hpp:695 -> 1555). Only a non-writing reader operation of an earlier layer's slot plus a preempted main thread could make it non-zero. Grade nit. Fix with one clause.

findings.title: T4 period keyed by operation change and filed under the last attention layer: two ops per layer or attention-free layers skew period_count/period_cycles
findings.trigger: An ingested model (a model whose per-model plugin code the ingest tool generated) whose schedule has two attention statements on one source layer (LoopyTron.hs:1041 sets attentionModelLayer from the statement's `layer`, and nextAttentionOpId gives each statement its own op id), or a hybrid model with attention-free layers between attention ops.
findings.consequence:
note_attn_job_entry_w0 closes a period on every op change (attn_stats.hpp:490-498) and adds it to timers_at(cls, t4_last_layer). Two ops on one layer give period_count 2 per forward for that layer and halve the mean. The time of consecutive attention-free layers is counted toward the last attention layer before them. The Note (the design comment block at the top of attn_stats.hpp) defines T4 by operations (attn_stats.hpp:36-38). So the code follows its definition. The leaf name period_cycles_w0 and the README's "layer period" wording assume one op per layer.
Current plugins: llama uses uniform bindings (common.hpp:259-262, op.i == layer.i). No such model was verified either way (Insufficient data: the list of ingested models with a non-uniform op-to-layer map).
findings.discriminating_check: grep the generated plugin of each shipped model for attention_binding{attention_op_id(N), model_layer_id(M), ...} and check whether any M repeats or any layer index is skipped. If neither happens in any shipped model, this is a sentence to add to the Note comment, not a code change.
findings.suggested_fix: Option 1: assert in note_attn_job_entry_w0 that a new operation also brings a new layer (TRON_ASSERT(layer != t4_last_layer) when t4_last_operation != NO_OPERATION). That assert makes a broken assumption abort the process. Option 2: state in the Note that T4 is per attention operation, and that the leaf keys it by the operation's model layer.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The T4 mechanism is as described, but the named trigger is not reachable. Torch-ingested models (models imported from PyTorch) number layers with a counter that increments once per attention op (ingest/src/TypedFxBulk.hs:190-204). Hand-written plugins use uniform bindings (kv_cache.hpp:448-452). So every shipped model has exactly one op per layer with no gaps. Only a hand-written --loopy-trace-file (JsonLoopy.hs:574, checked just for layer >= 0 at TronCheck.hs:601) or a future non-uniform plugin could reach it. A Note sentence or TRON_ASSERT(layer != t4_last_layer) is enough.
evidence: Holds as a future risk: the mechanism is confirmed by code at attn_stats.hpp:490-500, and the ingest checker (TronCheck.hs:600-602) does not forbid two attention statements sharing a model-layer id, nor skipped layers (LoopyTron.hs:155-171 handles non-dense writer layers). Correction: README.stats.md does not say "layer period". It says the T4 keys are "per layer" (README:281-283). The "layer period" phrase is in the Note at attn_stats.hpp:36 and self_attention.hpp:802.
intent: T4 is by design keyed by attention operation and filed under that operation's model layer (Note, attn_stats.hpp:36-38; PR body). No configured model has two ops on one layer or attention-free layers. So nothing is miscounted today. Drop the assert suggestion (it would abort production for a legal schedule). At most add to README.stats.md:282 that period_cycles_w0 spans from one operation's first job to the next operation's first job. A gap of attention-free layers then counts toward the preceding operation's layer.

findings.trigger: A break inside run_attention_job with the switch on: filing T2 under worker_ix instead of pool_worker_ix (self_attention.hpp:855), filing T3 for every worker instead of worker 0 (:856-857), or swapping attn_elapsed and t_end - t_entry. The only test that runs run_attention_job with a forward open (the Q-reuse (query reuse) section, a test section of t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp) uses the state's own stats object. That object follows TRON_ATTN_STATS and is off in CTest.
findings.consequence: Wrong per-worker rows, wrong per-layer T3/T4, or a swapped busy/wall pair in production would pass every CI test. The hooks themselves are asserted only in isolation (t_attn_stats.cpp:243-270).

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds: the only test that runs run_attention_job (heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:661/:708) uses the state's own switch-following object. So T2/T3/T4 filing (pool_worker_ix row, WORKER_0 gate, busy vs wall) is never checked through the production function. Caveat on the suggested fix: install_enabled_stats (:297-312) already calls begin_forward. So calling it before the forward_scope at :592 opens the forward twice. begin_forward has no re-entry assert (attn_stats.hpp:450-461). So the double open is harmless. To open the forward once, build the scope on the returned object, or split the helper. The W4 bounds assert is satisfied: attn.size() == app_pool().num_workers() (self_attention.hpp:480). So the 1-worker split files under row attn.size()-1.
evidence: Confirmed: the only executed run_attention_job calls with a forward open (heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:661 and :708) use the env-following stats object and assert nothing on the sums. So even the PR body's manual TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 test run would not catch a wrong row key, a wrong WORKER_0 gate, or swapped T2/T3 values. The suggested fix is feasible as written. begin_forward tolerates a second open. attn.size() equals app_pool().num_workers() (self_attention.hpp:480). So the last-row index matches pool_worker_ix.
intent: Holds: every stats-on test stops at apply_page_range or calls the hooks directly. So the pool_worker_ix expression (self_attention.hpp:797), the WORKER_0 gates (:803, :856) and the busy/wall pairing (:853-857) run under an enabled object only in the manual TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 pass. That pass asserts nothing about them. In the suggested fix the period checks must be cumulative over the two loop iterations (operation 1's layer == batch_ix + 1, operation 2's layer == batch_ix). The forward_scope at :592 then also exercises end_forward with an unknown split (folds all rows). That is fine.

findings.title: note_fpga_pass call site in prepare_uniform_hw_attention (K-token sum, per-layer filing) is executed by no unit test
findings.trigger: Any FPGA-assisted run: prepare_uniform_hw_attention runs with a non-empty hw_plan (the query batch's list of FPGA passes) and uses_hw, and TRON_ATTN_STATS=1.
findings.consequence: The formula fpga_k_tokens = sum over the pass's B queries (B = the number of queries in the FPGA pass) of (tok_ix_arr[qi] + 1) and the per-layer filing (fpga_at(current class, layer.i)) are verified only by hand on delphi-3bda (the Intel test machine with the FPGA cards), never by CI. A wrong relative index (e.g. an off-by-one in relative_hw_tok_ix's two return paths, or a loop bound other than B) would go unnoticed. The only tests of note_fpga_pass pass literal numbers to the hook (t/t_attn_stats.cpp:282-295, 869, 882).
findings.discriminating_check: Add a call of self_attn_state.prepare_uniform_hw_attention to the 'hardware attention configuration uses KV-slot identity' test (t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp). That test already has a fake PosDevice (the accelerator device interface of tron, here its in-process fake) and hw_attn_eligible == true. Use the hand-built two-pass plan (queries with known last_hw_token_pos over one fake shard, a shard being one token range of the KV cache held on one FPGA card). Then check fpga_at(cls, layer).k_tokens == sum of (expected relative index + 1) and query_passes == 2 x items.size(). If the fake device cannot run fill_attn_job_template / prepare_hardware_attn_job, assert the stats before that call by splitting the K-token sum into a small static helper and testing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Cover the call site once through the existing fake-device fixture (or factor the B-query K-token sum into a tiny inline helper next to relative_hw_tok_ix and test that helper with one pass of two shards and three queries, one per return path of relative_hw_tok_ix).

findings.title: On state: per-worker path_bits are small separate heap vectors; adjacent workers' buffers can share a cache line under the per-visit |=
findings.trigger: TRON_ATTN_STATS=1, decode forwards with few token jobs (e.g. 8 users -> 8-byte inner vectors). path_bits is `std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>>` (one heap buffer per pool worker, allocated by resize in begin_forward). glibc (the C library whose malloc hands out heap chunks) has a smallest chunk of 32 bytes. So two workers' 8-byte buffers can sit in one 64-byte line. Every visit does `path_bits[tok_ix.i] |= bit` (a byte read-modify-write) on the worker's own buffer, and the bit is already set after the first visit of that token job.
findings.consequence: On-state only: two attention workers whose buffers share a line move it between their caches once per visit (millions of visits per run). The PR's headon arms (the throughput runs of the PR head with TRON_ATTN_STATS=1) show no visible cost at 8 users (+0.39 % / -0.05 % TPS, tokens per second, relative to main with the variable unset). So this is a risk for larger worker counts or different allocators, not a measured defect. The off state is untouched (path_bits is nullptr and the block is skipped).
findings.evidence:

456-458: `    for (auto& bits : path_bits) {` / `      if (bits.size() < n_token_jobs) bits.resize(n_token_jobs, 0);` / `    }`
self_attention.hpp:1652: `            path_bits[tok_ix.i] |= attn_stats::path_bit(visit.served);`
findings.discriminating_check: With TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 print the addresses of path_bits[w].data() for consecutive attention workers (or run perf c2c, the Linux tool that reports cache-line sharing, on the headon arm). findings.suggested_fix: Allocate path_bits as one vector with a 64-byte-aligned stride per worker (max token jobs rounded up), or test before set (`if (!(b & bit)) b |= bit`) so the steady-state visit does a read only.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The buffers only grow (attn_stats.hpp:457). A prompt forward has one token job per prompt token (full.hpp:2115/2123). So after the first prompt longer than about 40 tokens every worker's buffer sits in its own >= 64-byte glibc chunk, and the decode-written prefix bytes no longer share a line. The risk is limited to processes whose forwards have all had <= 40 token jobs. The PR's headon arms (prompt lengths 1024 and 8192 tokens) never exercised that state. So they neither confirm nor bound it.
evidence: path_bits inner vectors grow to the largest job count of any forward (the first prompt forward, hundreds to thousands of bytes) and never shrink [attn_stats.hpp:456-458, :567-570]. So in production decode adjacent workers' written bytes are at least one buffer length apart and cannot share a cache line. The finding's "8-byte buffers" trigger exists only in a process that never ran a prompt forward (decode-only unit tests). The per-visit private-line RMW (read-modify-write) at self_attention.hpp:1652 remains, and its cost is smaller than the run-to-run variation of the measurement.
intent: Holds as an undocumented on-state future risk, not a design choice. The author put alignas(64) on worker_layer_row and layer_timers for exactly this reason (attn_stats.hpp:224-225, 252). path_bits stayed one small heap buffer per worker, written unconditionally on every visit (self_attention.hpp:1652). The one-line steady-state fix is to test before setting (`if (!(bits & bit)) bits |= bit`). That turns millions of stores into reads and needs no allocator assumptions. The measured headon cells (-0.05 / +0.70 / +0.39 % TPS at 8 users) show no cost today.

findings.title: Comment claims the destructor runs on exception unwinding, but forward() is noexcept
findings.trigger: Any exception thrown inside run_forward (not noexcept, model.hpp:1710) or its callees, for example std::bad_alloc from a vector resize, while TRON_ATTN_STATS=1.
findings.consequence: model::state::forward is declared noexcept (model.hpp:1653). An exception that reaches it calls std::terminate. The C++ standard does not guarantee stack unwinding before terminate in that case, and the common ABIs (application binary interfaces, here the GCC and Clang runtimes) do not unwind. So the sentence 'The destructor also runs when forward() unwinds through an exception, so such a forward is still counted' describes a path that does not exist. No counter is wrong. The comment promises a behavior the code cannot deliver.
findings.discriminating_check: Compile a tiny probe: a noexcept function that constructs an object with a printing destructor and then throws. With GCC or Clang the destructor output never appears before the terminate message. Or simply read model.hpp:1653: the noexcept on forward() shows that the sentence describes a path that cannot happen.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: 'forward() is noexcept and tron's asserts abort. So a forward that does not complete is never counted. There is no partial record.' Keep the rest of the paragraph.
lenses: FORWARD-PASS BOOKKEEPING: every entry point of a model forward at HEAD 04da001cb5, the forward_scope object, the class decision, the per-forward counters (forwards, T1, token_jobs, listener_jobs, kv_only_jobs, fpga_queries, token_jobs_by_path_set, n_attn_workers min/max), and the ordering between the main thread and the attention workers.
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Confirmed by a probe under tron's own compiler (clang 19.1.7 from nix, the package manager that supplies the build toolchain) and g++ 11.4, at optimization levels -O0 and -O2, with and without an outer catch. A local's destructor inside a noexcept function never runs before std::terminate. So the comment's unwinding sentence describes an impossible path. Soften the suggested replacement: say "forward() is noexcept and tron's asserts abort, so a forward that does not complete terminates the process and is never read", not "no partial record". The reason: note_attn_workers and the worker rows are written during the forward.
evidence: Confirmed by a probe built with the repo's own clang++-19 (and g++ 11.4). An exception escaping a noexcept function calls std::terminate with no destructor of that function's locals run. So ~forward_scope never executes on that path. The fix is comment-only. The second half of the sentence (tron's asserts abort, not throw) is correct per h/common/assert.hpp:59-62.
intent: Holds as a comment-only nit. forward() is noexcept [model.hpp:1653]. So an exception escaping run_forward terminates without unwinding, and ~forward_scope never runs. The sentence at attn_stats.hpp:864-866 promises a path that does not exist. This is not a documented design choice (Wade's W2, the README and the PR body say nothing about exceptions). Replace the sentence with "forward() is noexcept and tron's asserts abort, so a forward that does not complete is never counted."

findings.title: fpga_queries would double count if a plugin ran assemble_attention_plan twice in one forward
findings.trigger: A plugin (handwritten or generated) that calls assemble_attention_plan more than once inside one run(), for example to re-plan after a split change. Today llama.hpp:596 and the generated run() prologue (TronCpp.hs:1214) call it exactly once per forward. So the condition is not reached.
findings.consequence: assemble_attention_plan_impl calls construct_hw_plan per minibatch (one group of the forward's token jobs that is planned together) (model.hpp:2313). construct_hw_plan calls note_fpga_query per token job with an FPGA pass (model.hpp:2752). fpga_bits[job] = PATH_BIT_FPGA_4 is idempotent (a repeat has no further effect), but fpga_queries.fetch_add(1) is not. A second plan run adds the same jobs again. note_attn_workers (model.hpp:2303) would also record the split twice (harmless: min/max). Nothing detects the second call.
findings.discriminating_check: On the raw object: begin_forward, note_fpga_query(1) twice, end_forward. fpga_queries reads 2 while token_jobs_by_path_set['fpga'] reads 1. With the derived form below both read 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Either derive fpga_queries in end_forward (count the fpga_bits entries equal to PATH_BIT_FPGA_4, one add per forward, no mid-forward writer), or add TRON_ASSERT_EQ(forward_n_attn_workers, UNKNOWN_SPLIT) at the top of note_attn_workers so a second plan per forward aborts.
lenses: FORWARD-PASS BOOKKEEPING: every entry point of a model forward at HEAD 04da001cb5, the forward_scope object, the class decision, the per-forward counters (forwards, T1, token_jobs, listener_jobs, kv_only_jobs, fpga_queries, token_jobs_by_path_set, n_attn_workers min/max), and the ordering between the main thread and the attention workers.
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Unreachable at HEAD: both production callers of assemble_attention_plan (llama.hpp:596, generated run() prologue from TronCpp.hs:1214) run once per forward, and run_forward is called once per forward (model.hpp:1704-1711). The cheap guard TRON_ASSERT_EQ(forward_n_attn_workers, UNKNOWN_SPLIT) at the top of note_attn_workers (attn_stats.hpp:467) would match the W4 assert style and turn the once-per-forward contract into a checked one.

findings.title: fpga_query_passes counts logical passes, not physical hardware subcommands
findings.trigger: A pass whose shard span needs head tiling or more than one EMEM window: hw_pass.physical_subpasses > 1 (model.hpp:2726-2727). A shard is a fixed-length token slice of the KV cache on the card, and the shard span is the range of shards one pass covers. Head tiling splits the heads into smaller groups. EMEM is the FPGA memory that holds the intermediate Q-K dot products during hardware attention (libpos.hpp:129).
findings.consequence: note_fpga_pass files one (pass, query) pair per logical hw_pass. The card executes physical_subpasses commands for it. A reader comparing fpga_query_passes with FPGA command counters (or with the per-subpass decode work in try_unpack_hw_pass) sees fewer passes. Neither the hpp comment nor the README says which notion of pass is counted. Not a defect: the K-token count is the same either way.

common.hpp:748: size_t physical_subpasses = 1;               // EMEM-safe HW executions to join

The stats value is smaller by the subpass factor.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as a documentation nit, with two corrections. Head tiling does NOT create extra subcommands (a tiled span is one physical command, libpos.hpp:212-213). subcmds > 1 comes only from an untiled span wider than the EMEM shard cap (EMEM = the FPGA on-card memory that holds the intermediate Q-K scores; a shard = one 1024-token slice of the KV cache; libpos.hpp:215, e.g. more than 4 shards at 32 heads). The proposed perfetto check cannot show the gap. All subcommands of a pass run inside one attn_launcher (self_attention.hpp:716, worker.cpp:894-896). The discriminating number is sum over passes of pass.physical_subpasses * B (B = the number of query activations batched into one hardware command, at most 32; model.hpp:2729) versus query_passes.
evidence: Holds as a doc/design note, with two corrections. Head tiling that engages yields ONE physical command (libpos.hpp:213-215). So physical_subpasses > 1 needs covered_shards above the EMEM cap with tiling off or no legal tile. The perfetto attn_launcher_cb event (self_attention.hpp:716) is per logical pass too. So the discriminating check must count the worker's num_hw_subcmds (src/pos/worker.cpp:893) or acmds, not launcher events. The quoted comment is at attn_stats.hpp:265-267.
intent: Holds as an undocumented unit choice, with two corrections. Head tiling collapses a long span into ONE physical command (libpos.hpp:212-215). So physical_subpasses > 1 needs the span past the untiled EMEM cap with tiling off or no legal tile (at most 4 physical subpasses per pass, libpos.hpp:37). The perfetto 'hwattention' events are per logical pass (self_attention.hpp:716 attn_launcher_cb 'pass', pi). So the check must compare against driver-level counts (worker.cpp:893-898 num_hw_subcmds / :1207 result blocks per Q), not that track. attn_stats.hpp:123 already ties the count to hw_workload.passes. Only a 'whatever number of physical subcommands it takes' clause is missing at attn_stats.hpp:271-273 and README.stats.md:267.

reach: Holds: the uses_hw=true instantiation (t_llama_unit.cpp:2981) runs both the HW-range dismissal (step 7, 80 >= 64 threshold) and the empty visits of HW-owned pages (step 11 split, 40 < 64) but reads the state's env-driven stats object, so CI asserts only rows.empty(). The suggested assertion needs two corrections: the counter is visits[PASS_READY_0][visit_path::empty] (no 'ready_empty_visits' exists), and it is > 0 only after the split call of step 11; after the single call of step 7 it must be 0 because the HW range is dismissed before any apply_page_tok.
evidence: The gap holds: with TRON_ATTN_STATS unset in CI, the only hardware-layer apply_page_range run (t_llama_unit.cpp:2981, <8,false,true>) asserts nothing beyond rows.empty(). But the suggested assertion is wrong for that fixture: its nine HW-owned pages are dismissed before any visit (self_attention.hpp:1582-1593), so an enabled stats object would record 0 empty visits and n_q_tokens-1 avx visits on the tail page; there is no `ready_empty_visits` field (use visits_all(IX_EMPTY_0)). intent: Holds as an info-level test gap, but the suggested assertion must follow the split call (t_llama_unit.cpp:2566-2572, 40 query-page pairs per worker), not the unsplit call at 2489-2493: there the 80-pair section turns on range dismissal (self_attention.hpp:1522, 1590) and the nine HW-owned pages produce zero visits, so 'ready_empty_visits > 0' would fail at 2497. findings.title: The README says the leaves read {} after the last state dies. The code makes them read {} after the newest registered state dies
findings.trigger: Two model_stats objects of the same model id and prefix are alive; the second registered one is destroyed while the first still lives (t_attn_stats.cpp:615-627 builds exactly this).
findings.consequence: The leaves read "{}" although a live state of that id exists, until that state re-registers. README.stats.md:270-273 says "After the last state is destroyed the leaves read {}", which promises the opposite. Not reachable in production: rinzler keeps one scheduler (one state) per model name (src/rinzler.cpp:1937), and runtron builds its per-batch states one after the other inside stream_generate (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1453-1466), so the earlier state is gone before the next registers.
findings.discriminating_check: Register two on-states of one id, destroy the second, read <prefix>/decode_like_totals: correct per README would be the first state's numbers; the code returns "{}" (the unit test at t/t_attn_stats.cpp:628 asserts the code's behavior).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword README.stats.md:272-273 and the comment at attn_stats.hpp:910-913 to "After the state that registered last is destroyed the leaves read {}" (or "the newest state"). No code change.
lenses: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as a README wording nit only: the trigger cannot occur in runtron (one state at a time, scheduler is a stream_generate local) or rinzler (schedulers never erased before exit). Related but distinct: rinzler may load two entries with the same exec slug but different weights (src/rinzler.cpp:2066-2068), giving two live states under one FUSE prefix where only the later-registered one is ever visible; the README's "takes the leaves over" sentence covers it but a reader may not expect it in rinzler. The header comment at attn_stats.hpp:910-913 already describes the mechanism correctly (callbacks replaced), so only README.stats.md:272-273 needs the reword.
evidence: Holds as a wording nit: the unit test at t/t_attn_stats.cpp:615-630 already documents and asserts the code's actual rule (leaves read {} once the most recently registered state dies, even if an older one lives), so only the README sentence at README.stats.md:272-273 and the comment at attn_stats.hpp:910-911 need "the state that registered last" in place of "the last state" / "the model state". The fuse_sysfs evidence lives at src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:150-158 and :987-996.
intent: Only README.stats.md:272-273 needs rewording ("after the state that registered last is destroyed"); the header comment at attn_stats.hpp:910-913 already describes the real mechanism (callbacks replaced, weak_ptr of the registering state) and the unit test at t/t_attn_stats.cpp:614-628 asserts the code's behavior, so this is a known, deliberate takeover rule with one imprecise README sentence, unreachable in rinzler (one scheduler per model name) and runtron (sequential stream_generate calls; the EAGLE draft uses attention_eagle/).

findings.lens: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.title: ~model_stats and the stderr report can run on the FUSE thread when a read overlaps state destruction
findings.trigger: runtron keeps the FUSE tree mounted until main exits (src/runtron.cpp:485 unmount_guard), and destroys the model state after each prompt batch (h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1462-1466). A FUSE read of any attention leaf executes weak.lock() (attn_stats.hpp:931). If the main thread drops the last strong reference (self_attention::state member, self_attention.hpp:477) after that lock succeeded, the FUSE worker thread becomes the last owner.
findings.consequence:
The render finishes on a live object (no use-after-free). Then the shared_ptr in the callback releases. ~model_stats runs on the FUSE worker thread (attn_stats.hpp:388-390). print_report writes the [attn-stats] lines (log lines that carry the PR's [attn-stats] prefix) to stderr from there, after and possibly interleaved with runtron's own end-of-run output.
The FUSE design note asks callbacks to be quick (doc/fuse_stats_design.md:96). The report is a few KB of fprintf.
No data race: the report reads relaxed atomics (atomic loads with no ordering guarantee) of an object no other thread references any more.
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:388-390: "~model_stats() { if (enabled) print_report(stderr); }"
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:930-932: "[weak, render](...) { if (auto s = weak.lock()) return fuse::fuse_sysfs::value_type(render(*s)); ..."
src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:731-735: "{ std::shared_lock<std::shared_mutex> lock(node->structure_mutex_); read_callback = node->read_callback_; } if (read_callback) { value = read_callback(path, snapshot->value); }" (the callback runs outside every lock, on the FUSE thread)
src/runtron.cpp:485: "tron::fuse::stats::unmount_guard fuse_guard;" (unmount only when main returns)
findings.discriminating_check: Run runtron with TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 and --isolated-iterations 2 while a shell loop reads <prefix>/decode_like_totals continuously. A report line appearing after the next batch's "attention path stats on" info line (or from a thread id other than main under strace -f, the system-call tracer) shows the destructor ran on the FUSE thread. Correct-by-design behavior would still print once per state.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept and document in the Note (attn_stats.hpp:69-73): "the report prints when the last owner drops. A FUSE read that overlaps the state's destruction prints it from the FUSE thread." If a fixed thread is wanted, print from ~self_attention::state (call stats->print_report(stderr) there and make ~model_stats empty). The report then always runs on the destroying thread.
lenses: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Confirmed reachable in runtron only (rinzler keeps one state for the process lifetime). The window is the render time of a single leaf read that overlaps the end of a stream_generate batch. The consequence is limited to the [attn-stats] report printing from the FUSE thread after runtron's batch output. The Note in attn_stats.hpp:69-73 says "One summary goes to stderr when the model state is destroyed" and does not say which thread. The suggested doc sentence or printing from ~self_attention::state both close it.
evidence: Holds at HEAD: the only strong owner is self_attention::state::stats (self_attention.hpp:475), and the FUSE read callback's weak.lock() (attn_stats.hpp:931) can become the last owner. So ~model_stats and its fprintf report (attn_stats.hpp:388-390, 815-849) can run on the FUSE thread. The state dies per batch at stream_generate.hpp:998 (shutdown_scheduler), not at the caller lines 1462-1466 the finding cites. It is memory-safe as written. So it stays info-level. The fix is a Note sentence at attn_stats.hpp:70-73 or printing from ~self_attention::state.
intent: Holds as an undocumented side effect of the documented weak_ptr scheme: the window is one render (microseconds) per state teardown, and it needs a reader polling a leaf at that instant. print_report calls no fuse:: or spdlog (the logging library) function. So the FUSE-thread destructor cannot deadlock or corrupt anything. README.stats.md:245-246 ("a batch runtron run ends before the tree can be read") understates this: a reader polling during the run can read every leaf, and can also become the printer of the report.

findings.lens: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.title: n_attn_workers_min can read as UINT64_MAX in a one-time window if the two relaxed stores (atomic writes with no ordering guarantee between them) are reordered
findings.trigger: First forward of a class: note_attn_workers stores min (from UINT64_MAX) and then max (from 0) as two relaxed stores (atomic writes with memory_order_relaxed, which promise no ordering against other variables) to two different atomics (attn_stats.hpp:472-473). render_forwards guards the min with "max == 0 ? 0 : min" (attn_stats.hpp:775-777), which assumes a reader that sees max > 0 also sees the new min.
findings.consequence: Relaxed stores to different atomic objects carry no ordering in the C++ memory model. A compiler may emit the max store first. x86 hardware keeps program store order. So this needs compiler reordering. A FUSE read in that window prints n_attn_workers_min = 18446744073709551615 once. Cosmetic, one forward, first forward only.
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:472-473: "min_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_min, n_attn_workers); max_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_max, n_attn_workers);"
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:774-777: "// UINT64_MAX is the \"no forward yet\" initial value of the minimum. load_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_max) == 0 ? 0 : load_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_min),"
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:180-189: max_relaxed/min_relaxed are load + store with memory_order_relaxed.
findings.discriminating_check: Inspect the generated code of note_attn_workers with objdump (the tool that prints a binary's machine code) for the order of the two stores. Or run a reader loop against the first forward under a build with -O3 (the compiler's highest standard optimization level) and look for the UINT64_MAX value. Correct behavior prints 0 or the real minimum only.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard on the field itself: "load_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_min) == UINT64_MAX ? 0 : load_relaxed(fc.n_attn_workers_min)" at attn_stats.hpp:775-777. No ordering assumption then remains.
lenses: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The concurrent window itself is reachable (unlocked FUSE read callback at attn_stats.hpp:928-940 versus the main-thread store at model.hpp:2303). The wrong value needs the two relaxed stores or loads (atomic operations with memory_order_relaxed, which promise no ordering between them) to be observed out of program order. The C++ model allows that. x86 plus today's GCC and Clang (two C++ compilers) do not produce it. Guarding on the min field itself (UINT64_MAX, the largest 64-bit unsigned value, used here as the 'no value yet' marker) is a one-line fix that removes the assumption.
evidence: The window is symmetric: the reader's two relaxed loads (max at :775, min at :777) may also be reordered under the C++ model. So guarding on the min field itself (== UINT64_MAX) is the right fix regardless of the writer's store order. Only one such window exists per class over the process lifetime. The counters are never reset (attn_stats.hpp:71).
intent: The guard at attn_stats.hpp:775-777 reads the "no forward yet" state from a different atomic (max) than the one that holds the sentinel (min, the 'no value yet' marker). The two are written by two relaxed stores. The standard permits reordering on both writer and reader side. x86 store order and current GCC/Clang practice make the printed UINT64_MAX unobservable on the production target. So this is a one-line cleanup (guard on min == UINT64_MAX), not a defect.

findings.title: forward_scope holds a model_stats& while self_attention::state::stats is a replaceable shared_ptr
findings.trigger: A caller replaces state.self_attn_state.stats while a forward_scope built from the old object is open. Production never replaces it (the only assignment is the constructor, self_attention.hpp:495-498). Unit tests replace it (t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2615-2617, t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp) and t_llama_unit.cpp:2614 resets the scope first.
findings.consequence: If a future test or a hot-reload path replaced the shared_ptr with a scope open, ~forward_scope would write note_forward_wall/end_forward into a destroyed object. Today every replacement happens before the scope is created or after it is reset. So there is no defect.
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:867-871: "struct forward_scope : noncopyable<forward_scope> { model_stats& stats; const bool on; ..."
h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:476-477: "// ... (unit tests that never initialize the FUSE tree may replace it). std::shared_ptr<attn_stats::model_stats> stats;"
t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2614-2618: "stats_scope.reset(); state.self_attn_state.stats = std::make_shared<attn_stats::model_stats>(...); stats_scope.emplace(*state.self_attn_state.stats, ..."
findings.discriminating_check: Search for assignments to self_attn_state.stats outside constructors (grep "self_attn_state.stats ="): only tests. Each must precede scope creation or follow scope reset.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep as is. Optionally have forward_scope hold a std::shared_ptr<model_stats> (one reference-count increment per forward), so a replaced object outlives the scope. Or add a comment at attn_stats.hpp:868 that the referenced object must outlive the scope.
lenses: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as an informational design note only. The production forward_scope is a local of model::state::forward [model.hpp:1668], a member function of the state that owns the shared_ptr. So the referenced model_stats cannot be replaced or freed while the scope is open. All four test-side replacements (t_llama_unit.cpp:2185/2615, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:144, heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:309) happen before scope creation or after reset. No code change needed. A one-line lifetime comment at attn_stats.hpp:868 is the only optional action.
evidence: Holds as an info-level design note. All four replacement sites are tests, and each precedes scope creation or follows scope reset. The finding's trigger list omits t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:309 (install_enabled_stats). That helper also replaces the pointer, but with no forward_scope open (it calls begin_forward directly). Two transient locals `model_stats& stats_ref = *stats` at self_attention.hpp:803 and :1481 follow the same reference pattern within one call and add no new hazard.
intent: All four test-side replacements of self_attn_state.stats (t_llama_unit.cpp:2185, 2615; t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:144; heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:309 via sections 342/471) happen with no forward_scope open, and production assigns the member only in the state constructor (self_attention.hpp:495-498). The shared_ptr serves the FUSE weak_ptr callbacks, not scope lifetime. A one-line "must outlive the scope" comment at attn_stats.hpp:868 is the only thing worth adding.

findings.title: Takeover by a state with a different shape or switch leaves the earlier state's extra leaves installed
findings.trigger: register_fuse_files registers per-layer and per-worker leaves only when enabled (attn_stats.hpp:941-949) and never removes leaves. A later state of the same id and prefix with fewer layers, fewer pool workers, or the switch off would leave the earlier state's surplus leaves bound to the earlier weak_ptr.
findings.consequence: Those leaves keep reporting the earlier state (while it lives) or "{}" (after), next to a summary that describes the later state. Not reachable in production: TRON_ATTN_STATS is read once per process (attn_stats.hpp:161-172), the pool size is the process's app pool (self_attention.hpp:481, 496-497), and one process serves one model per id (src/rinzler.cpp:1937; h/runtron/stream_generate.hpp:1453-1466 uses one cfg).
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:941-949: "if (!stats->enabled) continue; for (size_t layer = 0; layer < stats->n_layers; ++layer) { leaf(...layer...) } for (size_t worker = 0; worker < stats->n_workers; ++worker) { leaf(...worker...) }"
src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:149-158: an existing path with the same read_only flag returns the existing handle ("if (it->second->is_read_only() == read_only) { return it->second; }").
findings.discriminating_check: In a unit test register an on-state with 4 layers then an off-state of the same id: decode_like_layer_0 still exists and reads the first state's numbers while summary says on:false.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Every cited code fact is correct, but no production path builds two states of one model id and prefix with a different switch, layer count or pool size. One guard the finding did not cite closes the only candidate route: get_scheduler asserts cfg.id == raw_model_name [src/tron/scheduler/legacy_dispatch.cpp:55]. A same-id state with a different layer count, pool size or switch cannot occur in one process (compile-time n_layers, process-global app_pool, once-per-process env_enabled, one config per id in rinzler and runtron). Optional one-line addition to the comment: "assumes the same shape and switch".

findings.title: render_summary reads get_cpu_freq(), a plain uint64_t published by the calibration thread
findings.trigger: A FUSE read of <prefix>/summary (attn_stats.hpp:733 calls hardware::system::get_cpu_freq()) while the TSC calibration thread updates detail::cpu_frequency_hz.
findings.consequence:
detail::cpu_frequency_hz is declared as a plain uint64_t (src/system/system.cpp:1794) and returned without synchronization (system.cpp:1897-1899). In the C++ memory model a concurrent plain write and read is a data race. On x86 a 64-bit aligned load is a single access. So the practical effect is at most a stale tsc_hz value.
This is pre-existing infrastructure (the same accessor serves cycles_to_ns everywhere). The PR only adds one more reader.
The writer side (system.cpp:1799-1803 comment about publish order) was not read for an atomic_ref.
findings.evidence:
h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:731-733: "... facts.page_size, n_workers, active_workers(), hardware::system::get_cpu_freq());"
src/system/system.cpp:1794: "uint64_t cpu_frequency_hz = 0;"
src/system/system.cpp:1897-1899: "uint64_t get_cpu_freq() noexcept { return detail::cpu_frequency_hz; }"
findings.discriminating_check: Read the writer at src/system/system.cpp:1799-1830. An std::atomic_ref or atomic store on cpu_frequency_hz removes the race. A plain assignment confirms the formal race (TSan, the ThreadSanitizer data-race detector, would report it on a FUSE read during calibration).
findings.suggested_fix: Out of scope for this PR. If the writer is plain, a follow-up can make detail::cpu_frequency_hz an std::atomic<uint64_t> with relaxed access in get_cpu_freq().
lenses: ASYNCHRONOUS OWNERSHIP AND CONCURRENCY (model_stats lifetime, FUSE leaf callbacks and takeover, forward_scope order versus pool workers, atomics and memory orders, torn reads (reads that see part of a value from before a write and part from after))
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The writer is a plain assignment (src/system/system.cpp:2019) inside a loop that runs every 50 ms for the process lifetime (system.cpp:1957-1958). So the formal race is confirmed, not hypothetical. It is pre-existing (cycles_to_ns at h/system/system.hpp:268 reads the same plain global). The PR only adds the FUSE-thread summary read. Its worst case on x86-64 is a tsc_hz value at most one 50 ms sample stale.
evidence: Writer confirmed plain: src/system/system.cpp:2019 "detail::cpu_frequency_hz = next_freq;" runs every calibration pass for the process lifetime. So the formal race is real, but it is pre-existing and untouched by this PR (no diff under src/system/). Precision: cycles_to_ns reads the variable directly (h/system/system.hpp:268), not via get_cpu_freq(). attn_stats.hpp:733 is the only get_cpu_freq() caller outside system.cpp.
intent: The writer is a plain store (src/system/system.cpp:2019). So the formal race is confirmed. It is pre-existing infrastructure shared by every cycles_to_ns caller (h/system/system.hpp:267-271). The repo already documents the same class of race for latest_tsc/latest_sys_ns (system.cpp:1975-1992). The PR only prints the value once in summary and documents the 0-before-calibration case (attn_stats.hpp:724-725). Worst case is a stale tsc_hz in one read, not a wrong counter. Follow-up outside this PR.

findings.title: The pool-worker mapping is computed by three formulas; note_attn_job uses the inline one
findings.trigger: run_attention_job computes pool_worker_ix inline from tp.num_workers() and files T2 with it. run_joins recomputes the same index through stats->pool_worker. apply_page_range uses stats_ref.pool_worker and, for the trace argument, the inline formula again.
findings.consequence: Two bases exist for the same index: the thread pool size (self_attention.hpp:797) and model_stats::n_workers, which is attn.size() at state construction (self_attention.hpp:496-498). / They are equal in production (attn.resize(app_pool().num_workers()) at self_attention.hpp:480, and the pool never resizes: threading.hpp:815-817 num_workers() = work_queues.size()). A test that grows attn (t_llama_unit.cpp:2603-2617) makes them differ. A future edit of one copy would not be caught by t_attn_stats.cpp. That test drives note_attn_job with a precomputed row (t_attn_stats.cpp:706-712).
findings.evidence: self_attention.hpp:797 'const size_t pool_worker_ix = tp.num_workers() - n_attn_workers + worker_ix;'; self_attention.hpp:855 'stats_ref.note_attn_job(pool_worker_ix, layer.i, attn_elapsed);'; self_attention.hpp:1342-1343 'stats->note_join_wait(\n            stats->pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers), layer.i, join_wait_cycles);'; self_attention.hpp:1485 'stats_enabled ? stats_ref.pool_worker(scratchpad, n_attn_workers)'; self_attention.hpp:1498 '"app thread id", app_pool().num_workers() - n_attn_workers + scratchpad,' (this line is pre-existing context in the diff); attn_stats.hpp:434 'return n_workers - n_attn_workers + attn_ix;'
findings.discriminating_check: Under TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 with n_main_helpers (the count of pool workers indexed below the attention workers) >= 1, read <class>_worker_<W> for W < n_workers - n_attn_workers_max: attn_jobs and busy_cycles must be 0 (T2 filed by the inline formula lands in the same rows as the visits filed by pool_worker). A wrong copy would show attn_jobs in a helper row with visits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the index once in run_attention_job as stats_ref.pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers) when stats are on (the speedometer, the pre-existing timing code at self_attention.hpp:837, keeps its own pool-size formula), and pass that pool index into run_joins instead of recomputing it there. Optionally TRON_ASSERT_EQ(stats->n_workers, app_pool().num_workers()) once at self_attention.hpp:498 to state the equality the hooks rely on.
lenses: Worker and layer indexing after W5 (commit bff317e0d3): row keying by pool worker, attention-index to pool-index mapping, split recording, active_workers, fold cost, per-worker leaves, boundary cases
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as a maintenance nit only. The inline formula at self_attention.hpp:797 is pre-existing code the PR reused for T2. The speedometer at :837 must keep the pool-size form. The thread pool never resizes (threading.hpp:763, :815-817). So no row can be misfiled today. The only place the two bases diverge is t_llama_unit.cpp:2603-2617, and that test never calls run_attention_job. The suggested fix reduces three formulas to two, not one.
evidence: Confirmed at HEAD: lines 797 and 1498 are pre-existing code, the PR adds the three hooks (855, 1342, 1485) that split the index across two bases. The grown-attn test (t_llama_unit.cpp:2603-2617) drives run_sections, not run_attention_job. So the inline formula at 797 runs only in production, where both bases are equal.
intent: Holds as a consistency nit. The T2 row at self_attention.hpp:855 reuses the pre-existing speedometer index (line 797, pool size). T5 (1343) and the visits (1485) go through model_stats::pool_worker (attn.size() at construction). The bases are equal in production, and the t_llama_unit growth test never reaches run_attention_job. So no number is wrong today. The suggested TRON_ASSERT_EQ at construction (line 498) would be a tautology. n_workers is attn.size() = app_pool().num_workers() there. The useful fix is to file T2 through stats_ref.pool_worker(worker_ix, n_attn_workers) under stats_enabled (which also asserts the pair fits the rows).

findings.lens: OFF-STATE COST AND HOT-LOOP CODE (TRON_ATTN_STATS unset must cost nothing measurable; per-visit / per-job / per-forward classification of every production line the PR adds to self_attention.hpp and model.hpp at HEAD 04da001cb5)
findings.title: Per-visit and per-call stats branches carry no tron_unlikely hint (the macro that tells the compiler a branch is rarely taken); layout of +141 on-state instructions is left to the compiler
findings.trigger: Any build. The visit loop of apply_page_range (384 instantiations, +47,276 bytes total per the PR body) contains the on-state block `if (stats_enabled) { stats_tally.record(...); path_bits[...] |= ...; }` at 1650-1653 and the per-call block at 1680-1685. Neither block carries a branch-probability hint.
findings.consequence: With the switch off, the hot loop executes one bool test per visit (as designed). But the compiler may lay the on-state code inline in the fall-through path (the code that follows the branch when it is not taken). That placement costs instruction-cache (icache) and fetch bandwidth in the most frequently executed loop of the program. The PR's own A/A shows code-placement effects of the same order as the resolution (+0.77 % TPS at prompt 8192 tokens, attributed to placement). model.hpp already uses `if tron_unlikely (cfg.log_intermediates)` for a directly analogous runtime switch.
findings.evidence:
1650: `          if (stats_enabled) {`
1651: `            stats_tally.record(visit.served, relevant_k_tokens, page::page_size);`
1652: `            path_bits[tok_ix.i] |= attn_stats::path_bit(visit.served);`
1680: `      if (stats_enabled) {`
h/common/attributes.hpp:65: `#define tron_unlikely(x) (x) [[unlikely]]`
h/tron/models/model.hpp:1208: `      if tron_unlikely (cfg.log_intermediates) {`
findings.discriminating_check: objdump the visit loop of the largest apply_page_range instantiation at HEAD. If the `record`/`|=` code sits between the apply_page_tok inline body and the loop back-edge (the jump back to the loop start, in the fall-through path), the hint moves it to a cold block (a code block placed away from the hot path). If it is already out-of-line (a jump to a block after the function's main body), the hint changes nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Write `if tron_unlikely (stats_enabled)` at 1650 and 1680 (and optionally at 854, 1275, 1341), matching model.hpp:1208.
lenses: OFF-STATE COST AND HOT-LOOP CODE (TRON_ATTN_STATS unset must cost nothing measurable; per-visit / per-job / per-forward classification of every production line the PR adds to self_attention.hpp and model.hpp at HEAD 04da001cb5)
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Discriminating check run on the local clang-19 (the C++ compiler, version 19) -O2 (its optimization level 2) object of model_llama_3p1_70b. The on-state block at self_attention.hpp:1650-1653 is laid out in the fall-through path (99 bytes at 0x2199-0x21fb, skipped by a taken `je`, the x86 jump-if-equal instruction, when the switch is off). So the hint `if tron_unlikely (stats_enabled)` would change the layout, as the finding says. The runtron binary the PR body measured was not inspected. Treat the production layout as inferred. Still a nit: one taken branch per visit, well inside the PR's measured band.
evidence: Confirmed by objdump of a HEAD-built object (clang-19, llama-3.1-8b, largest apply_page_range instantiation): the record/path_bits on-state block is one shared 145-byte block placed inline between the merged apply_page_tok return paths and the loop-continuation code, so the off state branches over it on every visit; `if tron_unlikely (stats_enabled)` at 1650 would let the compiler move it to a cold block. The gain is unmeasured, and the PR's off-state numbers are already inside the band. So this stays a nit.
intent: Confirmed by objdump of today's HEAD build (llama-8b object, clang 19): the off state jumps over a 145-byte inlined record block at +0x2793 on the main AVX visit path. So the hint would change layout. The A/A already shows the cost is below its 0.5-0.7 % TPS resolution, and no document records a decision against the hint. So this stays a consistency nit (model.hpp:1208 idiom), not a defect and not a documented design choice.

findings.lens: OFF-STATE COST AND HOT-LOOP CODE (TRON_ATTN_STATS unset must cost nothing measurable; per-visit / per-job / per-forward classification of every production line the PR adds to self_attention.hpp and model.hpp at HEAD 04da001cb5)
findings.title: Off state may pay one constant byte store per visit for page_tok_result::served beyond the bool test
findings.trigger: Switch off, any visit. apply_page_tok is TRON(inline) (always_inline) with three return points that each write a compile-time-constant `served` (amx at 1898, empty at 1950, avx at 1982). The only consumer is the `if (stats_enabled)` block at 1650-1653, and stats_enabled is a runtime value. So the compiler must keep `served` alive from the return point to the test. The one exception is a compiler that duplicates the block into each return path.
findings.consequence: If the compiler keeps `served` in a stack slot, the off state executes one `movb $const, N(%rsp)` per visit in addition to the one bool test. This is a private stack write, not a shared-memory write and not an atomic. So it does not break the 'no memory write to shared data' intent. But it is one instruction more than 'one bool test' if it happens. The PR's A/A (resolution ~0.5-0.7 %, the run-to-run spread of the measurement) cannot see it either way.
findings.evidence:
1645: `          const page_tok_result visit = apply_page_tok<geometry>(was_valid, page,`
1650-1652: `          if (stats_enabled) {` / `            stats_tally.record(visit.served, relevant_k_tokens, page::page_size);` / `            path_bits[tok_ix.i] |= attn_stats::path_bit(visit.served);`
1898: `          return {range_hint, int(page::page_size), attn_stats::visit_path::amx};`
1950: `        return {range_hint, 0, attn_stats::visit_path::empty};`
1982: `      return {range_hint, relevant_k_tokens, attn_stats::visit_path::avx};`
1837-1839: `    TRON(inline)` / `    page_tok_result apply_page_tok(bool was_valid,`
findings.discriminating_check: Run objdump -d (objdump = the GNU tool that prints the machine instructions of a compiled binary) on the largest apply_page_range instantiation at HEAD and look at the three inlined return points of apply_page_tok. A `movb $0x1`/`$0x2`/`$0x0, N(%rsp)` (a one-byte store to the stack, or a register move kept live to the `test`) before the jump to the common `if (stats_enabled)` test confirms the store. Three duplicated `if (stats_enabled)` tests with constant-folded record() calls refute it.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change is needed unless the objdump shows the store and someone wants it removed. In that case move the `if (stats_enabled)` record into each return path of apply_page_tok via a small inline hook that takes the constant path. The constant then folds away when off.
lenses: OFF-STATE COST AND HOT-LOOP CODE (TRON_ATTN_STATS unset must cost nothing measurable; per-visit / per-job / per-forward classification of every production line the PR adds to self_attention.hpp and model.hpp at HEAD 04da001cb5)
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: objdump of the HEAD build (clang 19, RelWithDebInfo = the CMake build type with optimization plus debug symbols, AMX-eligible h128/g4 bf16 instantiation: h128 = head size 128, g4 = 4 query heads per KV head, bf16 = 16-bit brain floating point) shows no stack store of `served`: the constant is packed into the register that already carries relevant_k_tokens, costing 2 register instructions on the AVX return (movabsq+orq), 0 on the AMX and empty returns, plus the one `cmpb $0,0xf(%rsp)` bool test. No memory write. Below A/A resolution. Measured on this build only, and the -O3 deb build (the Debian package build, compiled at optimization level -O3) may differ.
evidence: objdump of the HEAD build (llama-3-8b dtensor apply_page_range, clang 19 -O3) shows no stack store of `served`. Instead the compiler packs served into %rax (the return register) before the (5x duplicated) `stats_enabled` test. So in the off state an AMX visit pays 2 extra register instructions (movabs+add), an AVX visit 2 (movabs+or), and an empty visit 0, with no memory write. The suggested fix (fold record() into each return path so the constant dies when off) would remove those 2 instructions per visit. The cost is far below the A/A resolution and needs no action.
intent: Objdump of HEAD binaries (clang-19, RelWithDebInfo, AMX-eligible and non-AMX instantiations) shows no stack store of `served`: the compiler packs it into the rax return register with relevant_k_tokens, and each return path pays 0 to 2 register-only instructions plus the one `cmpb $0, N(%rsp)` bool test the contract already names. Not checked: the Release (-O3) deb preset. The objdump-check.sh recipe on that runtron would close it.

findings.title: register_fuse_files logs a 'takes over the leaves' info line and registers 5 leaves per model state even with the switch off
findings.trigger: TRON_ATTN_STATS unset, FUSE tree initialized (runtron dev build mounts <worktree>/stats/instance-N per the PR body's live-read section), and more than one model state constructed with the same model id in one process (the Note says runtron builds one state per prompt batch, attn_stats.hpp:72-73).
findings.consequence: Every state after the first logs `attention path stats: a new model state takes over the leaves under /model/<id>/attention` at info level. The line appears although nothing is collected. The summary, 2 totals and 2 forwards leaves are also (re)registered per state. No measurable perf cost (per model state, not per forward). The cost is one log line per model state after the first, in the off state. The PR describes the off state as costing nothing visible.
findings.evidence:
915: `inline void register_fuse_files(std::shared_ptr<model_stats> const& stats) {`
917: `  if (!fuse::stats::is_initialized()) return;`
921-925: `  if (fuse::stats::get_file_handle(prefix + "/summary")) {` / `    spdlog::info(` / `        "attention path stats: a new model state takes over the leaves under {}",` / `        prefix);` / `  }`
935-940: leaves for summary, <class>_totals, <class>_forwards registered before `if (!stats->enabled) continue;` at 941
self_attention.hpp:499: `        attn_stats::register_fuse_files(stats);` (unconditional in the state constructor)
findings.discriminating_check: Run runtron with two prompt batches (two model states), TRON_ATTN_STATS unset, dev-build FUSE mount present. Then grep the log for 'takes over the leaves'. One hit = confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the takeover log on `stats->enabled`, or lower it to spdlog::debug (the debug level of spdlog, the logging library). Keep the five off-state leaves if the README contract ('summary reports "on":false') is wanted.

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Reachable with the switch unset in any runtron run with more than one prompt batch. runtron builds one full_scheduler (the scheduler object that owns one model state) per batch (stream_generate.hpp:1460-1462 and :915). Each batch therefore gets its own model state. The reason: FUSE is initialized unconditionally (runtron.cpp:494, rinzler.cpp:4403), and the info line at attn_stats.hpp:921-925 checks only that the summary leaf already exists. The README (README.stats.md:271) documents the info line without an on-state restriction. So this is a documented design choice. The finding's "(re)registered" wording overstates it: make_file returns the existing handle, and only the callbacks are replaced.
evidence: The unconditional info line and the five off-state leaves are exactly as cited at attn_stats.hpp:921-925 and :935-941. But the line is documented behavior (README.stats.md:270-272, attn_stats.hpp:911-913). And the PR's "costs nothing" claim is about the A/A perf measurement (a throughput comparison of two arms that are expected to show no difference), not logs. findings.title: visit_tally (64 bytes) is zero-initialized on every apply_page_range call regardless of the switch
findings.trigger: Every apply_page_range call, switch on or off (about workers x kv_heads x layers x 2 passes calls per forward).

attn_stats.hpp:15: `// ... Per call the cost is one byte load and one stack tally.`

findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as a documented design choice: the 64-byte zero-init at self_attention.hpp:1483 runs on every apply_page_range call (run_sections:1176, every worker, layer and pass) with the switch off, and the Note at attn_stats.hpp:15 budgets exactly this ('one stack tally'). The 'compiler cannot elide it' clause and the 'eight 8-byte stores' form are unverified (no objdump run). The cost is not measurable against the A/A band either way.
evidence: Confirmed at HEAD: the 64-byte tally at self_attention.hpp:1483 is zeroed once per apply_page_range call before the switch is tested, and the Note (attn_stats.hpp:15) already declares it. intent: Confirmed by objdump of the HEAD build (t_llama_unit.cpp.o, RelWithDebInfo). It sits between the `enabled` byte load and the `cmp $0x1,%cl` switch test. So it runs on every apply_page_range call with the switch off. This is exactly what the Note in attn_stats.hpp:15 documents ("one byte load and one stack tally"). So it is a documented design choice, not a defect.

findings.title: The pool-row keying checks in t_llama_unit degrade to WARN, not a failure, on a one-worker pool
findings.trigger: A host or slice where app_pool().num_workers() == 1.

findings.title: Note memory line counts rows and timers only; path_bits and fpga_bits scratch is not mentioned
findings.trigger: Switch on, a forward with many token jobs (a prefill chunk, a prompt-processing slice of thousands of tokens) on a pool of n_workers (the pool worker count).
findings.consequence: begin_forward grows every path_bits vector to n_token_jobs bytes and never shrinks it. So the on-state memory is rows + timers + n_workers x max(n_token_jobs) + max(n_token_jobs) bytes. The Note's 'Memory when on' sentence names the first two terms only. For 27 workers and a 8192-token chunk that is about 230 KB more, the same order as the 373 KB rows figure.
findings.evidence: attn_stats.hpp:83-85: `Memory when on: 2 classes x pool workers x layers x 192 bytes of rows, for / example 27 x 36 x 2 x 192 = 373 KB, plus 2 x layers x 64 bytes of timers.` attn_stats.hpp:426-429: `fpga_bits.assign(n_token_jobs, 0); for (auto& bits : path_bits) { if (bits.size() < n_token_jobs) bits.resize(n_token_jobs, 0); }`.
findings.discriminating_check: After a forward with N token jobs, path_bits[w].capacity() >= N for every w. The Note's figure does not include it.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'plus (pool workers + 1) x the largest forward's token jobs in bytes of path-bit scratch'.
lenses: DOCUMENTATION AND EXPORTED VALUES (README.stats.md attention section, Note [Attention path stats] and other comments in attn_stats.hpp, JSON keys rendered by render_summary/render_totals/render_forwards/render_layer/render_worker/print_report, FUSE leaf names, live PR body at HEAD 04da001cb5)
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Confirmed: attn_stats.hpp:83-84 counts rows and timers only. begin_forward (attn_stats.hpp:455-458) grows path_bits to (pool workers) x N bytes plus fpga_bits N bytes and never shrinks them. So a switch-on run that once saw an N-token-job forward keeps about (pool workers + 1) x N bytes extra (229 KB for 27 workers x 8192 jobs). Only the Note is affected. README.stats.md and the PR body state no memory figure.
evidence: Holds at HEAD. The resize evidence is at attn_stats.hpp:455-458 (not 426-429). The scratch is grown for all n_workers pool workers (constructor sizes path_bits to n_workers at :380). So the added term is (pool workers + 1) x the largest forward's token-job count in bytes, kept until the model state is destroyed.
intent: Holds: the Note names the scratch (path bits, FPGA bits) at line 64-65, but the memory sentence at line 83-84 counts rows and timers only. The scratch is (pool workers + 1) x largest n_token_jobs bytes, never shrunk, plus the small fpga counter array (2 x layers x sizeof(layer_fpga_counters)). The 230 KB example assumes a forward of 8192 token jobs. This check did not confirm 8192 as the production maximum. The fix is one appended clause either way.

findings.title: render_summary embeds model_id unescaped; the stderr report path has no is_safe_model_id guard
findings.trigger: A model state whose cfg.id (h/tron/models/config.hpp:20) contains a double quote, backslash or control character, built with TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 and at least one forward. The summary goes to stderr at state destruction.
findings.consequence: The FUSE leaves are protected (register_fuse_files returns early at L918), but print_report at L829-830 prints render_summary() for any id. The `[attn-stats] model ...: {...}` line is then not valid JSON. A script that parses the stderr report (the PR's campaign scripts read these lines) then breaks. Whether an ingested id can contain such a character is not established from the code read here.
findings.evidence:
L727-731: `"{{\"on\":{},\"model_id\":\"{}\",\"eagle\":{},...` with `enabled, model_id, is_eagle, ...` and no escaping
L829-830: `std::fprintf(f, "\n[attn-stats] model %s: %s\n", model_id.c_str(), render_summary().c_str());`
L918: `if (!is_safe_model_id(stats->model_id)) return;` (guards the FUSE path only)

findings.suggested_fix: Option 1: escape the id in render_summary (fmt, the formatting library, with a small escape helper). Option 2: store a sanitized copy at construction when is_safe_model_id fails (for example replace the offending characters with '_' and log once). Either way both the leaf and the report then use a safe string.

The campaign scripts parse the totals/forwards lines, not the summary line. So the stated script breakage does not apply.

findings.title: 'prompt chunk' carries two meanings in the listener comment of forward_counters
findings.trigger: A reader of attn_stats.hpp:286-288 interpreting listener_jobs for a long prompt.
findings.consequence: The comment says the last token of a prompt chunk has a listener with an empty logits (per-word scores) buffer, and in the next sentence that a chunk cut by the per-forward token limit has no listener in that forward. In the code a listener is attached once per extend request node [src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:191-192]. An extend request is one request that adds tokens to a user's sequence, and the node is its entry in the token tree (tron's tree of all users' token sequences, distinct from the FUSE tree of leaves). The listener is registered only when the whole edge (the node's run of tokens) was processed in this forward [full.hpp:2455-2459]. So 'chunk' means an extend request in one sentence and a forward cut in the next. The README (README.stats.md:250-252) defines chunk as 'the slice of a prompt that one forward processes'. That definition matches only the second meaning.
findings.discriminating_check: Ask whether a 4096-token prompt sent as one request and cut by live_token_limit into 4 forwards produces 1 listener (code) or 4 (first sentence of the comment).
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'the last token of one extend request (a node) has a listener. A request cut over several forwards by the per-forward token limit registers it in the forward that finishes the node'. Keep 'chunk' for the forward cut as the README does.
lenses: CONDITION MATRIX (boundary and mode coverage) for PR 4596 at HEAD 04da001cb5

findings.title: Draft-model forwards after a sampling round carry KV-only jobs; README 'every generated token has one' holds for the target model only
findings.trigger: Speculation on (legacy_dispatch.cpp:68-73 attaches a speculator scheduler when an eagle model exists). Read the draft/EAGLE model's own attn-stats leaves (a separate model_stats per model state, self_attention.hpp:496-498). Two cases. / (a) Separate draft model: the last draft layer is lazy (speculate.cpp:630-643, lazy_sequence_prompt only records lazy_tokens). When sampling accepts a path ending at a last-layer node, the next draft_step extends from get_location_speculator(current), and its lazy_tokens hold that token. full.cpp:109-115 prepends the lazy tokens to the new edge. findings.consequence: In the draft model's leaves the first draft step of every round is classified prompt_or_mixed (n_listeners < n_token_jobs), although no prompt is involved and all jobs are generated tokens. README.stats.md:254 says listener_jobs covers 'every generated token', and the Note/PR body describe decode_like as 'one generated token per user'. Both are true for the target model and false for the draft/EAGLE model's stats. The target model's verify forward itself is decode_like (see verified_correct).

findings.trigger: A future change to compute_forward_args that registers a listener for a node without pushing (or reusing) a token job in the same frame, or that visits a node twice. Today no such path exists (the verified_correct section shows this). So the trigger is hypothetical.
findings.consequence: gather_token_job_ids (model.hpp:1796-1816) would still pass. token_job_id_of_token[tok] of a token without a job reads a zero-initialized token_job_id (line 1799-1801 resizes with default values). has_listener[...] = 1 twice is silent. begin_forward's TRON_ASSERT_LE(n_listeners, n_token_jobs) (attn_stats.hpp:452) is only a count bound.
