findings.title: Generated plugins: stats 'layer' is the attention-op ordinal (nextLayer counter), not the model's layer index
findings.trigger: Any ingested model. TypedFxBulk (the ingest module that converts the model's traced graph) assigns the ModelLayerId of each TronSDPA (one attention operation node of that graph) from a per-function counter. The counter increments once per attention operation. The model's own layer_idx is not used. The generated plugin's n_layers (row count, facts.n_layers) is num_hidden_layers from the config.
findings.consequence:
For every ingested model at HEAD (one attention per hidden layer: qwen-3-4b, gpt-oss, gemma-3/4, mixtral, ...) the ordinal equals the hidden-layer index. So rows, note_fpga_pass filing and the T4 key are correct. The README/Note wording 'per layer', 'model layer' and the leaf key layer_<l> describe the l-th attention operation, which is what the code keys by. A future ingested model with attention-free hidden layers would file the l-th attention op under layer l (not under its hidden-layer index) with no error.
A future explicit-cache model (a plugin that lists its KV cache slot per attention operation) with two attention ops in one hidden layer would have n_attention_ops > n_layers. Then model_layer.i would reach n_layers. row()/timers_at()/fpga_at() abort on that value with the switch on (attn_stats.hpp:395/409/419). The off state is unaffected. The uniform-cache case is caught at compile time (kv slot = model layer, n_slots = n_layers, kv_cache.hpp:375).
findings.evidence: TypedFxBulk.hs:199-204 `nextLayer :: ConvertM Integer` / `let layer = currentLayer s` / `modify $ \s -> s{currentLayer = layer + 1}`; TypedFxBulk.hs:909 `layer <- nextLayer`, :919 `pure $ B.Attention qVar kvAccessVars layer geometry attnType mSinksVar attentionScale`; LoopyTron.hs:1041 `let modelLayer = T.ModelLayerId layer`, :1062 `T.attentionModelLayer = modelLayer`; Tron.hs:761-763 `-- | Diagnostic identity of the source model layer. This is deliberately distinct from 'AttentionOpId'`; Loopy.hs:390-391 `(Variable "n_layers" IntType Nothing) ["num_hidden_layers"]`; self_attention.hpp:206 `static constexpr size_t n_layers = plugin::n_layers;`, :492 `facts.n_layers = n_layers;`, :498 `attn.size(), n_layers);`; attn_stats.hpp:395 `TRON_ASSERT_LT(layer, n_layers);`; kv_cache.hpp:375 `if (operation.binding.kv_slot.i >= n_slots ||`; common.hpp:259-262 `uniform_attention_binding(...) { return {operation, model_layer_id(operation.i), kv_slot_id(operation.i)}; }` (llama plugin: same ordinal identity); gemma4_export.py:207 `"Gemma-4 attention stack has duplicate layer indices: ..."` (export rejects two attention modules with one layer_idx)
findings.discriminating_check: Ingest a model whose Fx trace (the PyTorch FX graph of the model that the ingest tool reads) has two TronSDPA ops in one decoder block (or one block without attention) and read the generated plugin's attention_operations array: model_layer_id values are 0,1,2,... in trace order regardless of the block index. With TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 and n_attention_ops > num_hidden_layers the state constructor's rows are too few. The first add_visits/note_attn_job_entry_w0 on the extra operation then aborts on TRON_ASSERT_LT(layer, n_layers).
findings.suggested_fix: One sentence in README.stats.md and in Note [Attention path stats]: 'layer_<l> is the l-th attention operation of the plugin's schedule (model_layer_id). For every current plugin this equals the model's layer index.' Optionally size rows by plugin_t::attention_operations.size() instead of plugin::n_layers. Then the row bound follows the operation table (the value that binding.model_layer.i is derived from) rather than the config's layer count.

findings.title: help_drain_gof: attention workers do GOF populate + DMA-submit work between jobs, outside T2 and T3, inside T4, on both plugins
findings.trigger: FPGA-assisted run with pending KV transfers (gof_coop_queue_ non-empty). Generated path: TronCpp.hs emits outer_state.help_drain_gof(4) before every run_attention_job (attentionWorkerOperation). Llama path: begin_attention_job calls enclosing_state.help_drain_gof(4) before run_attention_job. Both sit before the T3 t_entry stamp at self_attention.hpp:805-806.
findings.consequence: Up to four fire_gof_rodeo calls per attention worker per operation (real work: GOF populate and DMA submit, model.hpp:3134-3140) are counted in no timer. T4 minus T3 on worker 0 contains this work plus the phase-barrier wait (wait_attention_job / free_scratchpads_barrier.wait) plus the attn_done_barrier wait of finish_attention_job. The README's T5/T2/T3 sentences do not mention it, so a reader of the FPGA-assisted leaves cannot separate 'worker waited' from 'worker did DMA work' in the T4-T3 residue. This extends the already-reported 'T3 and T4 have different job boundaries' item with a concrete non-wait component; it is not a plugin asymmetry (both plugins place it identically).

findings.lens: fuse-mounted-read-path (second round): the mounted FUSE read/getattr path that executes the attn_stats leaf callbacks in rinzler and runtron, the singleton lifecycle, and the enumerators of /model/
findings.title: A mounted read re-renders per read() call; a growing leaf can deliver extra tail bytes to a two-call reader
findings.trigger: Stats on, engine under load. A reader (every `cat`, and any loop that reads until EOF, the end of the file) issues read() #1. op_read serves that call from one rendering. The reader then issues read() #2 at offset = that length to detect EOF. Between the two calls a counter in the leaf crosses a power of ten (visits 999 -> 1000, cycles 10^13, ...). So the second rendering is longer.
findings.evidence: src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:725-745: `auto snapshot = node->get_active_data(); value_type value = snapshot->value; ... if (read_callback) { value = read_callback(path, snapshot->value); } std::string content = fs->value_to_string(value) + "\n"; if (offset >= static_cast<off_t>(content.size())) { return 0; } size_t available = content.size() - offset; size_t to_read = std::min(size, available); memcpy(buf, content.c_str() + offset, to_read);` -- the callback runs before the offset check on every call. src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:710-711: `fi->direct_io = 1; fi->keep_cache = 0;` (no page cache, every read() reaches op_read). src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:623-635: op_getattr calls `read_callback(path, snapshot->value)` again and sets `stbuf->st_size = content.size() + 1`. h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:931-934: the leaf lambda renders live on each call.
findings.discriminating_check: On a mounted tree with TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 under load, run `for i in $(seq 100000); do cat <mount>/model/<id>/attention/decode_like_layer_0 | python3 -c 'import sys,json; json.load(sys.stdin)' || echo BAD; done`. Any BAD line is this behavior. A single-read reader (`dd bs=1M count=1`) never shows it.
findings.suggested_fix: No code change needed in this PR. Add one README.stats.md sentence. It says: read a leaf with one read() call or tolerate trailing bytes. The reason is that the tree renders live on every read. A fuse_sysfs-level fix (render once per open and keep it behind fi->fh) is a separate change.
lenses: fuse-mounted-read-path (second round): the mounted FUSE read/getattr path that executes the attn_stats leaf callbacks in rinzler and runtron, the singleton lifecycle, and the enumerators of /model/
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The mechanism is real and reachable (direct_io + per-call re-render + counters that only grow). But it is pre-existing fuse_sysfs behavior shared by every live read-callback leaf (expert_stats.hpp:158/184/192 has the same pattern), and fuse_sysfs.cpp is unchanged by this PR. The failure needs a digit-count change within the microseconds between two read() syscalls. That makes it rare. The shrinking case (offset past the new end) is harmless (returns 0). A one-sentence README note is the proportionate response.
evidence: Holds, with a sharper trigger. A single counter gaining a digit adds one byte. The extra tail is then only "\n", and the result is still valid JSON. A two-call reader gets invalid JSON only when the rendering grows by two or more bytes between its two read() syscalls (two counters changing digit count at once, or a state takeover flipping "{}" to a full rendering). fuse_sysfs.cpp is unchanged by this PR (getattr st_size at :638, direct_io at :710-711 pre-exist). The README sentence is therefore the only in-PR action.
intent: Pre-existing shared FUSE-layer behavior (fuse_sysfs.cpp is not in this PR, and expert_stats and rinzler callback leaves have the same property). A single digit crossing between the two read() calls adds only a trailing "\n". JSON parsers accept that. Invalid JSON needs two or more counters to cross a digit boundary in the same microseconds. A reader that uses a small buffer (dd bs=1) gets bytes from different renderings, the same root cause. The README sentence should therefore say: read a leaf with one read() call.

findings.title: op_read and op_getattr do not catch a throwing read callback; get_value does
findings.trigger: A render_* call on the FUSE thread throws. The only throw site is allocation inside fmt::format_to into a std::string (std::bad_alloc). tron asserts abort rather than throw.
findings.consequence:
The exception leaves op_read/op_getattr. These are static C++ functions called from C code in libfuse (the C library that implements the FUSE file-system side). That C code has no unwind tables (the data a C++ exception needs to pass through a function). So the process terminates instead of the read failing. The unit-test path (file_handle::get_value) catches and returns the stored value. So tests cannot show the asymmetry.
This is pre-existing for every callback leaf (the expert_stats leaf router_N/counts, which reports the expert-router counts, uses the same shape). This PR adds between 5 (summary plus the totals and forwards leaves of both classes) and 2*(2+n_layers+n_workers)+1 (with every layer and worker row present) such leaves per model state.
findings.evidence: src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:736-737: `if (read_callback) { value = read_callback(path, snapshot->value); }` (no try). src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:632-633: same in op_getattr. src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:944-950: `if (cb) { try { return cb(path_, snapshot->value); } catch (...) { return snapshot->value; } }`. h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:722-737: render_summary is not noexcept and uses `fmt::format_to(std::back_inserter(out), ...)`.
findings.discriminating_check: Read the three call sites: the asymmetry is visible in the code. Reachability needs an allocation failure on the FUSE thread. No in-repo test provokes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Out of scope for this PR. If wanted, wrap the callback in op_read/op_getattr the way get_value does, in fuse_sysfs.cpp.
lenses: fuse-mounted-read-path (second round): the mounted FUSE read/getattr path that executes the attn_stats leaf callbacks in rinzler and runtron, the singleton lifecycle, and the enumerators of /model/
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: The uncaught-callback asymmetry is real (fuse_sysfs.cpp:632-633, :734-735 vs :944-948). But op_read/op_getattr already build std::string outside any try for every leaf (fuse_sysfs.cpp:635, :737). So a bad_alloc (the C++ exception thrown when memory allocation fails) on the FUSE thread terminates the process with or without this PR's callbacks. The only reachable trigger is heap exhaustion, and fuse_sysfs.cpp is outside the PR. Not a PR defect. Pre-existing, informational.
evidence: Holds exactly as stated at HEAD. The only throw site is std::bad_alloc inside fmt::format_to (format strings are literals, TRON_ASSERT aborts). So this is a pre-existing fuse_sysfs.cpp property that the PR only multiplies in leaf count, not a defect introduced by the PR. The "without unwind tables" parenthetical does not matter. With or without them, no handler exists on the libfuse thread. So the process terminates either way.
intent: Holds and is pre-existing in the FUSE layer (expert_stats and rinzler callbacks share the same shape). The only throw in the PR's renderers is std::bad_alloc from fmt::format_to into a std::string. So the practical exposure is an out-of-memory FUSE read, and that read would terminate the process either way. The "without unwind tables" phrase is unverified but irrelevant. No handler exists on the libfuse thread. So std::terminate follows regardless.

findings.title: Size test cites fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH as a leaf constraint, but the read path never applies it
findings.trigger: Reading t_attn_stats.cpp:509-513 or a future contributor sizing a new leaf.
findings.consequence: The comment says every leaf 'must keep ... below fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH'. fuse_sysfs (the code module of tron's FUSE layer) enforces that constant only on op_write (returns the -E2BIG error code) and file_handle::set_value (returns false). The callback result in op_read, op_getattr and get_value is delivered whole, and the header says make_file itself allows a longer string. The assertion is a self-imposed budget, not a contract of the FUSE layer. The stated reason is wrong.
findings.evidence: t/t_attn_stats.cpp:511-513: `// A large model shape: many workers and layers must keep every leaf below // fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH, because every leaf is one layer or one // worker, never the whole table.` and :551 `CHECK(s->size() < tron::fuse::fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH);`. src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:804 `if (str.size() > fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH) { return -E2BIG; }` (op_write) and :904 (set_value) are the only two uses. h/system/fuse_sysfs.hpp:58-59: `// When value_type is a std::string, exceeding MAX_STRING_LENGTH is allowed // (e.g. a possibly long readme) with make_file`. src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:725-745 (op_read) has no length check.
findings.discriminating_check: grep -n MAX_STRING_LENGTH src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp shows only lines 804 and 904, both on the write side.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment: the limit is a size budget chosen so one leaf fits one FUSE read request. fuse_sysfs does not truncate callback output. Or keep the check and cite the reason (one read() call returns the whole leaf).
lenses: fuse-mounted-read-path (second round): the mounted FUSE read/getattr path that executes the attn_stats leaf callbacks in rinzler and runtron, the singleton lifecycle, and the enumerators of /model/
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Confirmed: attn_stats leaves are read-callback leaves [attn_stats.hpp:928-932]. fuse_sysfs applies MAX_STRING_LENGTH only on op_write (:804) and set_value (:904), never to callback output in op_read/op_getattr. So word it as a self-chosen size budget. (2) h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:667-668 carries the softer "stays well below fuse_sysfs::MAX_STRING_LENGTH" and can stay or be reworded the same way.

findings.title: Running t_llama_unit as root now aborts the whole binary at the first FUSE case (fuse_sysfs root assert)
findings.trigger: geteuid() == 0 when t_llama_unit runs (a root shell, or a container whose user maps to uid 0). The first stats_environment case (t_attn_stats.cpp:589) calls tron::fuse::stats::initialize(dir), which constructs fuse_sysfs.
findings.consequence:
fuse_sysfs's constructor runs a TRON_ASSERT against uid 0 outside any fork. So the process aborts. Every later case of t_llama_unit (the [attn_stats] cases at 637 and 903, and any case ordered after them) is lost. Before the PR t_llama_unit never constructed a fuse_sysfs. The property is new to this binary.
Precedent: t_tronstats_convention.cpp:167 initializes the same singleton and has the same property. So this is a known class of problem in the repo, not a new class.
findings.evidence: t/t_attn_stats.cpp:104 `tron::fuse::stats::initialize(dir);`; h/system/fuse_stats.hpp:42 `instance_ = std::make_unique<fuse_sysfs>(std::forward<Args>(args)...);`; src/system/fuse_sysfs.cpp:117 `TRON_ASSERT((getuid() != 0) && (geteuid() != 0), "fuse_sysfs must not run as root");`; h/common/assert.hpp:59-62 tron_abort ends in `std::abort();`. This machine runs as uid 644434775 (`id -u`). So the local run is unaffected.
findings.discriminating_check: `sudo -E ./gen/t_llama_unit "[attn_stats]"` aborts with 'fuse_sysfs must not run as root' at the first FUSE case; the same command as a normal user passes all 19 cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the three FUSE cases with Catch2 (the C++ unit-test framework of the repo) SKIP() when geteuid() == 0, or leave as is and state the root restriction in the t_attn_stats.cpp header comment.
lenses: t-llama-unit-binary-interactions
findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds as stated. Two additional points. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build (assert.hpp:3-4 undefines NDEBUG). So no release configuration avoids the abort. The repo already guards root with Catch2 SKIP() in t_cache_fs.cpp:216-217 and t_hwperf.cpp:408. So a three-line `if (::geteuid() == 0) SKIP(...)` in stats_environment matches existing convention. findings.title: rinzler stderr report prints during static destruction, after the tree is unmounted, via drogon's controller registry
findings.trigger:
rinzler stopped by SIGTERM/SIGINT (a stop from platformd, the host service that manages rinzler, or from systemctl): the loop poll calls stats::unmount() then app().quit() (rinzler.cpp:4801-4808). The --port-file failure path does the same (rinzler.cpp:4759-4761).
The completions_controller that owns every scheduler (rinzler.cpp:1937, 2337) has two owners. One is the local shared_ptr at 4623. The other is the function-local static map of drogon (the HTTP server library), filled through app().registerController(controller) at 4666 (DrClassMap.cc:25-30, 97-103). So ~completions_controller (rinzler.cpp:2457-2465), and with it ~model::state -> ~model_stats -> print_report(stderr) (attn_stats.hpp:388-390), runs only after main returns, during static destruction.
findings.consequence: The report is not lost by design: print_report uses std::fprintf on stderr and fmt only (attn_stats.hpp:816-848), no spdlog (the logging library), and stderr is open during static destruction. But three limits remain. / (1) The leaves are already gone when the state dies. So the README's 'when the model state is destroyed' event is invisible to any FUSE reader in rinzler, and the only rinzler output is this stderr text. / (2) The report depends on the pre-existing rinzler static-destruction teardown (shutdown_scheduler -> work_barrier on a function-local static work queue, full.cpp:414-418) reaching the attention state without an earlier abort. This review could not run that teardown. / (3) A SIGKILL after systemd's stop timeout drops the report. No code change in this PR alters that order.

rinzler.cpp:4666 `app().registerController(controller);`

rinzler.cpp:2459-2463 `// Clean up all schedulers  for (auto& [_, scheduler] : schedulers) { if (scheduler) { shutdown_scheduler(scheduler, shutdown_type::halt); } }`
attn_stats.hpp:388-390 `~model_stats() { if (enabled) print_report(stderr); }`
findings.discriminating_check: Stop a TRON_ATTN_STATS=1 rinzler with SIGTERM and read the journal (the systemd log). The '[attn-stats] model' lines must appear after 'Rinzler shutting down. Removed PID file' (printed inside ~completions_controller at rinzler.cpp:2474) and after the FUSE mountpoint is gone. findings.suggested_fix: Add one README sentence: in rinzler the stderr summary appears at process exit, after the stats tree is unmounted. So an interval read must be taken before the stop. findings.verifier_notes:
reach: Holds: in rinzler the only owner of the model state that outlives main() is drogon's static controller map. So the stderr summary prints during static destruction after stats::unmount(). The static-init order (work queue built inside the controller constructor, drogon map first touched at registerController) makes that teardown reach the state without a destroyed-queue hazard. Minor citation fixes: signal poll block is rinzler.cpp:4802-4809 and the 'Removed PID file' line is 2475. The README sentence at README.stats.md:244-246 is accurate but silent on the rinzler timing.
evidence: Holds at HEAD: the stderr report is emitted from member destruction of ~completions_controller (scheduler map -> full_scheduler::state -> self_attn_state.stats). So a teardown abort is unlikely, though this was not run here.
